pm_structure.summary: Group-level, outsourced construct: Primerica's investment committee (senior management) sets guidelines; a single unnamed third-party investment advisor manages the invested-asset portfolio and reports to the committee. Canadian-dollar assets are held within the group portfolio to back Canadian liabilities; there is no Canadian investment team or affiliated asset manager. Canadian segregated funds (legacy Common Sense Funds) use a third-party advisor for asset allocation; Canadian mutual-fund distribution relies on AGF and Mackenzie as manufacturers.
bullets: Conservative strategy: preservation of capital and liquidity; limits on asset type, issuer, credit quality, duration and country
Portfolio (Jun 30 2026, group US$4.1bn): public corporates 45.2%, MBS 15.8%, cash & equivalents 14.6%, private placements 8.7%, ABS 6.0%, government 5.6%, CMBS 1.9%, munis 1.1%, equities 0.3%
Ratings (amortised cost): AAA 18.4%, AA 13.6%, A 24.8%, BBB 42.4%, below IG 0.9%; duration 5.2y; book yield 4.4%
Term-life model means little spread/accumulation business: profitability less sensitive to investment income than peers

PFSL Fund Management Ltd. (Canadian fund manager) manages legacy Concert Series funds with a third-party advisor on allocation; PFSL Investments Canada is exclusive principal distributor of AGF and Mackenzie FuturePath 'PD Funds'
Seg funds: legacy Common Sense Funds underwritten by PLICC (sales fell sharply after June 2023 regulatory changes); since 2025 Primerica distributes Canada Life seg-fund contracts instead

rotation_commentary.text: Group portfolio grew to US$4.1bn; unrealised loss US$140mm is rate-driven, intent and ability to hold to maturity; growth in invested assets lifted net investment income (Q2 2026 NII US$43.7mm vs 40.9).
Primerica Life Canada statutory capital rose to US$903.3mm from US$696.2mm while paying US$45.3mm dividends; dividend capacity US$215.7mm at Jan 1 2026.
Shift of Canadian seg-fund business from PLICC's own Common Sense Funds to distributing Canada Life contracts (rolled out 2025) reduces PLICC's seg-fund growth and fee base.

notes: Primerica Life Canada is a captive term-life underwriter inside a US distribution company: Canada is ~13% of group revenue (US$441mm) and ~14% of pre-tax income, with statutory capital of US$903mm and an upstream dividend of US$45mm in 2025. There is no Canadian investment function; the group's US$4.1bn portfolio (99% fixed income, A average, 5.2y duration, 42% BBB) is run by an unnamed third-party advisor under a management investment committee, with CAD assets earmarked against CAD reserves. Parent leverage is a single US$600mm 2.80% 2031 note (bookrunners Wells, Citi, JPM, BNY, Goldman, RBC, Scotia) plus a US-only XXX surplus-note structure. Sources: Primerica, Inc. FY2025 10-K (Feb 2026), Q2 2026 10-Q (Aug 2026), 2026 proxy (Apr 2, 2026), Investor Update 2Q26, Q2 2026 earnings release, Nov 2021 424B5 prospectus supplement.
